quizzes.question: A pointer is a variable that stores a memory address.
quizzes.explanation: A pointer stores the memory address of another variable.

quizzes.question: In int *p;, *p is the name of the pointer variable.
quizzes.explanation: p is the name of the pointer variable, and * indicates that it is a pointer.

quizzes.question: The & operator returns the address of a variable.
quizzes.explanation: & is the address-of operator that returns the memory address of a variable.

quizzes.question: The * operator accesses the value that a pointer points to.
quizzes.explanation: * is the dereference operator that reads the value at the address a pointer points to.

quizzes.question: A NULL pointer is a pointer that points to nothing.
The size of a pointer varies depending on the data type it points to.
quizzes.explanation: Pointer size is the same regardless of the data type, determined by the system architecture (32-bit: 4 bytes, 64-bit: 8 bytes).

quizzes.question: In pointer arithmetic, p+1 always increases the address by 1.
quizzes.explanation: p+1 increases the address by the size of the data type it points to.

quizzes.question: A void pointer can store the address of any type.
quizzes.explanation: void* is a generic pointer that can store the address of any data type.

quizzes.question: The name of an array is the address of its first element.
quizzes.explanation: An array name represents the starting address of the array.

quizzes.question: An uninitialized pointer points to NULL.
quizzes.explanation: An uninitialized pointer contains a garbage value (dangling pointer).
